findings.value: WHY CLEANNESS IS NECESSARY: not for the person's own benefit but RELATIONALLY. The purpose-coding across the book returns BELONGING first (be holy as I am holy; that you should be mine - 20:26), then PROTECT-THE-HOLY (a holy God dwells in the midst; uncleanness would defile his sanctuary and kill - 15:31), then ACCESS (to approach / eat the holy - 22:4-7) and DANGER-AVERSION (lest they die). Cleanness exists because the Holy One dwells among them and they are HIS.

WHERE UNCLEAN COMES FROM: the source-coding clusters at the boundaries of LIFE and DEATH - the corpse (mortuary), the body's life-fluids and their loss (discharge, menstruation, semen, childbirth = genital-bodily), disease as a living-death (skin-disease/tzaraat, the largest bodily source), and the table (dietary) - together with MORAL/CULTIC rupture (sin, sexual sin, idolatry, sacrilege), which is the single largest source-domain (164 spans). The common thread: contact with death or loss of life-wholeness, and moral fault. Uncleanness is what is incompatible with the God of life.

WHY COVER, NOT SCRUB (the key finding): the RESET is graded by GRAVITY, and the RESULT-WORD is domain-specific. Light contact uncleanness (carcass, corpse, menstrual-contact) is reset by SCRUBBING + WAITING alone (wash/launder/until-evening) - never covering. Graver states (skin-disease, abnormal discharge, childbirth) AND all MORAL fault require BLOOD/ATONEMENT (kaphar = literally 'to cover') + sacrifice. The mechanism (cover) can be shared, but the OUTCOME differs by state: bodily defilement ends in TAHER (you are CLEAN); moral fault ends in SALACH (you are FORGIVEN). You are made clean of the body, forgiven of sin - two categorically different resolutions. The Day of Atonement (16:30) is the single bridge verse where cleansing-language (taher) is applied to sin. So covering is reserved for what a wash cannot reach: the deep, the persistent, and the moral.

IS CLEANNESS IB-DESIRE, EXTERNAL, OR PREREQUISITE: it is NEVER driven by the inner being's own desire - the driver-coding returns ZERO volition. It is EXTERNAL COMMAND (141 spans) or DIVINE-INITIATIVE (19; 'I the LORD sanctify you' 20:8). The person is roughly half PASSIVE (atonement done FOR him) and half ACTIVE (he washes, confesses, afflicts himself). Cleanness is a required PREREQUISITE for belonging and access, imposed by the holy God's presence - the self does not want it for its own sake; it is owed to the God who dwells there.

DOES AWARENESS COME IN (the key split): awareness is DECISIVE for MORAL fault but IRRELEVANT for BODILY uncleanness. Moral sin is not activated or remediable until KNOWN - the ch4-5 pattern runs hidden (alam) -> 'when he comes to know it' -> realizes his guilt -> confesses (yadah). Bodily uncleanness, by contrast, defiles AUTOMATICALLY (awareness 'not-in-view' on every genital/mortuary/dietary occurrence) whether or not one knows. So the inner being's KNOWLEDGE matters only where the fault is moral; the body's states run mechanically. Guilt engages the interior; defilement does not.

PAST-ONLY OR FORWARD: cleanness is MOMENTARY and PAST-DIRECTED - a repeatedly-restored baseline (until-evening, or a fixed 7/33/66-day period), constantly re-incurred and re-remedied, never a secured forward state. Dietary and disease classifications are STANDING (inherent to the animal / the condition). Moral atonement is RECURRING (the annual Day). By sharp contrast HOLINESS (the holy axis) is STANDING-FORWARD - a vocation to be maintained ('you shall be holy'). So the two must not be confused: CLEAN = a momentary reset of the immediate past; HOLY = a maintained forward standing.

THE SELF IN LEVITICUS is the NEPHESH - the living person/self held in a STATE - NOT the deliberating HEART. nephesh runs to ~50 spans in every sense (person, self, life, the-dead, life-in-blood); the heart (levav) appears only THREE times in the whole book (19:17 'do not hate your brother in your heart'; 26:36 a 'faint heart' in exile; 26:41 the 'uncircumcised heart' humbled). Leviticus does not psychologise the interior; it locates the person as a STATUS-BEARING SELF. And the state is borne not only by persons (377) but by objects, houses, land, garments, and the sanctuary itself - the inner condition is ENVIRONMENTAL as much as internal: a person, a people, a place can all be clean/unclean/holy.

ATONEMENT WORKS BY LIFE: kaphar (cover) is not lexical cleansing - it is the substitution of a LIFE. 'The life (nephesh) of the flesh is in the blood; I have given it on the altar to make atonement for your souls (nephesh); it is the blood that atones by the life' (17:11,14). Atonement covers the person by a life given for a life. On the Day of Atonement three distinct mechanisms operate together: kaphar (cover by blood), taher (cleanse), and the scapegoat that BEARS AWAY the confessed iniquity (avon) into the wilderness (16:21-22). The atonement/ritual words are thus the MECHANISM of reset - not themselves the inner-being state; the inner-being terminology is the clean/sin state that the mechanism resets (confirming the researcher's opening hypothesis).

LEVITICUS DOES REVEAL A DIVINE INTERIOR - and it is the axis the whole system turns on. God has a nephesh (soul) that ABHORS or does-not-abhor his people (26:11 'my soul shall not abhor you'; 26:30 'my soul will abhor you'); a FURY/wrath (chemah 26:28); a settled PLEASURE in the rightly-given offering (the 'soothing/pleasing aroma' nichoach, 16 occurrences, and its withdrawal 26:31 'I will not smell your pleasing aromas'); and a REMEMBERING of the covenant that is the ground of all restoration (26:42,45). The clean/holy/sin system exists because a holy God with a real, responsive disposition dwells IN THE MIDST - the inner being the book most fully portrays is God's.

THE INNER BEING'S OWN ACT AND THE WAY BACK: the people's ONE required interior act in the whole ritual system is SELF-AFFLICTION - 'you shall afflict your souls' (anah nephesh) on the Day of Atonement (16:29-31; 23:27-32), an active self-denial, cut off if withheld. And the way back from the covenant-curse is wholly INTERIOR: they must CONFESS their iniquity (yadah) and their uncircumcised HEART be HUMBLED (kana, 26:40-41) - whereupon God REMEMBERS the covenant. Where the ritual acts on the person from outside (washing, blood, atonement done FOR him), these two - self-affliction and confessing/humbled repentance - are the inner being's own active turning, and they are the hinge on which mercy swings.
